The *Ekavihāriyattheragāthā* ("Verses of the Elder Ekavihāriya") is a canonical poem preserved in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 10.2), situated within the Sutta Piṭaka's collection of early Buddhist verse [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records ten translations across nine languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No curated parallels in other early Buddhist canonical collections are registered on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal matches in commentarial literature, including ten matching segments shared with the second volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (with the longest alignment spanning verses §0.4–6.4) and thirteen segments recurring in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (notably §10.3–10.5) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring machine alignments across languages with the Tibetan translation of the *Samādhisambhāraparivarta-nāma* (D 3924), matching nine segments including §4.4 [DharmaNexus].
